## Purpose

This document examines population growth, PSP/MSA spatial boundaries and long-term urban expansion across Melbourne's fringe growth areas.

## Packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(terra)
```

## Data

```{r}
population <- read_csv(
  "data/meeting1/abs_erp_population_2001_2025.csv"
)

msa <- read_csv(
  "data/meeting1/msa_precinct_attributes.csv"
)

lga_boundary <- st_read(
  "data/LGA_2025_AUST_GDA2020/LGA_2025_AUST_GDA2020.shp",
  quiet = TRUE
)

# Create study LGAs
study_lga <- lga_boundary |>
  filter(LGA_NAME25 %in% c(
    "Casey", "Hume", "Melton", "Whittlesea", "Wyndham"
  ))
```

## Population growth

```{r}
population_growth <- population |>
  filter(year %in% c(2001, 2025)) |>
  select(council, year, population) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = year,
    values_from = population
  ) |>
  mutate(
    growth = `2025` - `2001`,
    growth_percent = growth / `2001` * 100
  )

population_growth
```

Population growth provides broader context for increasing development pressure across the five fringe LGAs.

## PSP/MSA spatial processing

```{r}
# PSP boundary
psp_boundary <- st_read(
  "data/PSP_Boundary/PSP_Boundary.geojson",
  quiet = TRUE
)

# Check unmatched PSP names
anti_join(
  msa |> distinct(psp_name),
  psp_boundary |> st_drop_geometry() |> distinct(PSP_NAME),
  by = c("psp_name" = "PSP_NAME")
)

anti_join(
  psp_boundary |> st_drop_geometry() |> distinct(PSP_NAME),
  msa |> distinct(psp_name),
  by = c("PSP_NAME" = "psp_name")
)

# Standardise PSP names
psp_boundary <- psp_boundary |>
  mutate(
    PSP_NAME = case_when(
      PSP_NAME == "Quandong PSP (Council-led)" ~ "Quandong PSP",
      PSP_NAME == "Croskell" ~ "Croskell (Casey Central)",
      TRUE ~ PSP_NAME
    )
  )

# Join MSA attributes to PSP boundary
msa_spatial <- msa |>
  left_join(
    psp_boundary,
    by = c("psp_name" = "PSP_NAME")
  ) |>
  st_as_sf()

# Check unmatched MSA precincts
msa_spatial |>
  filter(st_is_empty(geometry)) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(psp_name, lga, subregion, type)
```

Of the 122 MSA records, 117 were successfully matched to PSP polygons after standardising two inconsistent precinct names. Five precincts remain unmatched.

```{r}
# Keep matched PSP/MSA precincts
msa_matched <- msa_spatial |>
  filter(!st_is_empty(geometry))

# Transform to Victorian Land Cover CRS
msa_vicgrid <- st_transform(msa_matched, 3111)

# Create the five-LGA study area
study_lga_vicgrid <- st_transform(study_lga, 3111)

study_area <- study_lga_vicgrid |>
  st_union()

# Calculate original precinct area
msa_full_area <- msa_vicgrid |>
  mutate(
    full_area_ha =
      as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 10000
  ) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(
    psp_name,
    full_area_ha
  )

# Clip precincts to the five-LGA study area
msa_study <- suppressWarnings(
  st_intersection(
    msa_vicgrid,
    study_area
  )
)

# Calculate proportion of each precinct inside the study area
msa_study <- msa_study |>
  mutate(
    study_area_ha =
      as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 10000
  ) |>
  left_join(
    msa_full_area,
    by = "psp_name"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    study_overlap_percent =
      study_area_ha / full_area_ha * 100
  )

# Keep precincts with substantial overlap
msa_study <- msa_study |>
  filter(
    study_overlap_percent >= 50
  )

stopifnot(
  n_distinct(msa_study$psp_name) == 101
)
```

Of the 117 matched PSP/MSA precincts, 105 intersect the five study LGAs. Four precincts overlap the study area only marginally (<0.3% of their original area) and are treated as boundary slivers. Precincts with at least 50% of their original area inside the five-LGA study area are retained, leaving 101 precincts for precinct-level analysis.

## Urban expansion analysis

```{r}
# Land Cover Time Series
landcover_files <- list.files(
  "data/VIC_LANDCOVER_TS",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

periods <- c(
  "1985-90", "1990-95", "1995-00", "2000-05",
  "2005-10", "2010-15", "2015-19"
)
```

### LGA-level urban expansion

```{r}
# Calculate urban area by LGA
get_urban_area <- function(file, period) {

  landcover <- rast(file)

  landcover_study <- crop(
    landcover,
    vect(study_lga_vicgrid)
  ) |>
    mask(vect(study_lga_vicgrid))

# Built environment and urban area
  urban <- landcover_study %in% c(1, 2)

  urban_lga <- extract(
    urban,
    vect(study_lga_vicgrid),
    fun = sum,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

# Each 25 m x 25 m cell equals 0.0625 hectares
  study_lga_vicgrid |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    select(LGA_NAME25) |>
    bind_cols(urban_lga) |>
    select(-ID) |>
    rename(urban_cells = 2) |>
    mutate(
      period = period,
      urban_area_ha = urban_cells * 0.0625
    )
}

urban_change <- map2_dfr(
  landcover_files,
  periods,
  get_urban_area
)

urban_change
```

```{r}
# Urban expansion
urban_growth <- urban_change |>
  filter(period %in% c("1985-90", "2015-19")) |>
  select(LGA_NAME25, period, urban_area_ha) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = period,
    values_from = urban_area_ha
  ) |>
  mutate(
    growth_ha = `2015-19` - `1985-90`,
    growth_percent = if_else(
      `1985-90` > 0,
      growth_ha / `1985-90` * 100,
      NA_real_
    )
  )
urban_growth
```

Urban land increased across all five study LGAs. Casey had the largest absolute increase, while Melton had the largest proportional increase.

```{r}
# Urban land trend
ggplot(
  urban_change,
  aes(
    x = period,
    y = urban_area_ha,
    group = LGA_NAME25,
    colour = LGA_NAME25
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Urban land area over time",
    x = "Period",
    y = "Urban area (ha)",
    colour = "LGA"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### PSP/MSA-level urban expansion

```{r}
# Calculate urban area by PSP/MSA precinct
get_psp_urban_area <- function(file, period) {

  landcover <- rast(file)

  landcover_psp <- crop(
    landcover,
    vect(msa_study)
  )

# Built environment and urban area
  urban <- landcover_psp %in% c(1, 2)

  urban_psp <- extract(
    urban,
    vect(msa_study),
    fun = sum,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

# Each 25 m x 25 m cell equals 0.0625 hectares
  msa_study |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    select(psp_name, lga, subregion, type) |>
    bind_cols(urban_psp) |>
    select(-ID) |>
    rename(urban_cells = 5) |>
    mutate(
      period = period,
      urban_area_ha = urban_cells * 0.0625
    )
}

psp_urban_change <- map2_dfr(
  landcover_files,
  periods,
  get_psp_urban_area
)

nrow(psp_urban_change)
```

```{r}
# PSP/MSA urban growth
psp_urban_growth <- psp_urban_change |>
  filter(period %in% c("1985-90", "2015-19")) |>
  select(psp_name, lga, subregion, type, period, urban_area_ha) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = period,
    values_from = urban_area_ha
  ) |>
  mutate(
    growth_ha = `2015-19` - `1985-90`,
    growth_percent = if_else(
      `1985-90` > 0,
      growth_ha / `1985-90` * 100,
      NA_real_
    )
  )

head(psp_urban_growth, 10)
```

```{r}
# Calculate precinct area
psp_area <- msa_study |>
  mutate(
    psp_area_ha = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 10000
  ) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(psp_name, psp_area_ha)

# Add precinct area and urban land share
psp_urban_growth <- psp_urban_growth |>
  left_join(
    psp_area,
    by = "psp_name"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    urban_share_1985 = `1985-90` / psp_area_ha * 100,
    urban_share_2015 = `2015-19` / psp_area_ha * 100,
    urban_share_change = urban_share_2015 - urban_share_1985
  )

psp_urban_growth
```

```{r}
# Precincts with the largest absolute urban growth
top_psp_growth <- psp_urban_growth |>
  arrange(desc(growth_ha)) |>
  select(
    psp_name,
    lga,
    `1985-90`,
    `2015-19`,
    growth_ha,
    growth_percent
  ) |>
  head(10)

top_psp_growth
```

```{r}
# Top 10 precincts by absolute urban growth
ggplot(
  top_psp_growth,
  aes(
    x = reorder(psp_name, growth_ha),
    y = growth_ha
  )
) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 PSP/MSA precincts by urban land growth",
    x = "PSP/MSA precinct",
    y = "Urban land growth (ha)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Top 10 precincts by change in urban land share
top_psp_share <- psp_urban_growth |>
  arrange(desc(urban_share_change)) |>
  head(10)

ggplot(
  top_psp_share,
  aes(
    x = reorder(psp_name, urban_share_change),
    y = urban_share_change
  )
) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 PSP/MSA precincts by change in urban land share",
    x = "PSP/MSA precinct",
    y = "Change in urban land share (percentage points)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Compare top precincts across the two development indicators
top_growth_names <- top_psp_growth |>
  select(psp_name) |>
  mutate(top_absolute_growth = TRUE)

top_share_names <- top_psp_share |>
  select(psp_name) |>
  mutate(top_share_change = TRUE)

top_indicator_comparison <- full_join(
  top_growth_names,
  top_share_names,
  by = "psp_name"
) |>
  mutate(
    top_absolute_growth = replace_na(top_absolute_growth, FALSE),
    top_share_change = replace_na(top_share_change, FALSE)
  )

top_indicator_comparison

# Precincts appearing in both top 10 lists
top_indicator_overlap <- top_indicator_comparison |>
  filter(top_absolute_growth, top_share_change)

top_indicator_overlap
```
The PSP/MSA-level analysis shows that urban expansion is unevenly distributed across the study area. Precincts such as Clyde Creek, Ravenhall (Quarry Site), Cranbourne East and East Werribee Employment Precinct show relatively large absolute increases in urban land between 1985–90 and 2015–19. However, the ranking changes when urban growth is measured relative to precinct size. Granite Hills, Robinsons Road Employment Area North and Collison Estate show particularly large increases in the share of land classified as urban.

Cranbourne North (Stage 1) and Greenvale Central are the only precincts that appear in the top 10 under both indicators. This suggests that absolute urban growth and change in urban land share capture different dimensions of development pressure. Both measures will therefore be retained for the next stage of the analysis, when development pressure is compared with threatened-species occurrence and biodiversity value.

```{r}
# Save processed development indicators
dir.create(
  "data/processed",
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

write_csv(
  psp_urban_growth,
  "data/processed/psp_urban_growth.csv"
)
```
